**[[Ecuadorian conflict (2024–present)|Ecuadorian conflict]]

'''Law and crime'''
*A [[Judiciary of Belgium|court]] in [[Brussels]], [[Belgium]], orders former diplomat [[Étienne Davignon]] to [[Adjudicative competence|stand trial]] on charges of participation in [[war crime]]s in connection with the 1961 killing of former [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese]] [[Prime Minister of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|prime minister]] [[Patrice Lumumba]]. Davignon is the only surviving individual among those accused by Lumumba’s family of involvement in the case. [https://www.caledonianrecord.com/news/national/belgian-diplomat-ordered-to-stand-trial-over-1961-congo-leader-murder/article_79ebcc10-59b9-5568-a762-3e6c21596918.html (AFP via ''The Caledonian-Record'')]
*A [[Vatican City|Vatican]] [[Law of Vatican City|appeals court]] orders a [[retrial]] of [[Cardinal (Catholic Church)|Cardinal]] [[Giovanni Angelo Becciu]], who was convicted of [[embezzlement]] in 2023, citing procedural errors in the original proceedings. The court maintains his previously imposed prison sentence pending the outcome of the new trial. [https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/world/980389/vatican-court-orders-embezzlement-re-trial-for-cardinal/story/ (AFP via GMA News)]
*The [[Legislative Assembly of El Salvador]] votes 59–1 to approve a [[Constitution of El Salvador|constitutional]] amendment to permit courts to issue sentences of [[life imprisonment]] to individuals convicted of [[murder]], [[rape]], or [[terrorism]] where the limit was previously 60 years. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/el-salvador-reforms-constitution-allow-life-sentences-2026-03-17/ (Reuters)]
*One person is killed and another is injured in a shooting at [[Holloman Air Force Base]] near [[Alamogordo, New Mexico|Alamogordo]], [[New Mexico]], [[United States]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/shooting-holloman-air-force-base-new-mexico/ (CBS News)]

**In [[association football]], the [[Confederation of African Football]] formally overturns the result of the [[2025 Africa Cup of Nations final]] in which [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]] won 1–0 over hosts [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]] due to a controversial walk-off by Senegalese players during [[Overtime (sports)|extra-time]].
